what: The boundary is a wall, not a target
title: The classic SESOI power analysis, and what it cannot tell you
text: Asking minimum-effect power SESOI statistically degenerate, powerape refuses explanation rather returning useless number: null boundary minimum-effect test, claim succeeds probability equal test size (2.5% 95% CI) sample size.
code: ape_power(d, n = 5000, claim = "minimum", sesoi = 0.05) #> Error: #> ! Assumed true APE (0.0500 in magnitude) does not exceed the SESOI (0.0500). On or below the null boundary of the minimum-effect test the claim succeeds with probability ~2.5% (the test size) at ANY sample size, so no n delivers meaningful power. Either assume a planning value above the SESOI, or run the classic SESOI analysis instead: claim = "detect" with the target set to the SESOI.

title: Powering for equivalence: showing an effect is too small to matter
text: Sometimes research goal show effect negligible: cheaper treatment meaningfully worse, feared side effect meaningfully present. equivalence claim succeeds whole confidence interval lies inside (-SESOI, +SESOI). non-significant test evidence absence; CI inside equivalence bounds . coherence guard requires |target| < SESOI: power equivalence assuming true effect beyond bounds.
code: library(powerape)  d <- ape_dgp(model = "probit",              focal = pa_var("treat", "binary", p = 0.5),              covariates = list(pa_var("age", "normal", mean = 45, sd = 12)),              baseline = 0.30, signal = 0.10) d <- set_ape(d, target = 0)    # planning value: no effect at all

title: Powering for equivalence: showing an effect is too small to matter
text: Equivalence needs CI narrow, just centered near zero, sample sizes driven entirely SESOI: halving SESOI roughly quadruples required n.
code: ape_power(d, n = 2000, claim = "equivalence", sesoi = 0.05,           nsim = 600, seed = 1) #> powerape -- equivalence claim (CI within +/-0.050) #>   probit, n = 2000, assumed true APE +0.0000, 95% CI, nsim = 600 #>   power = 0.417 (MCSE 0.020) #>   outcomes: minimum 0.000 | detect-only 0.018 | inconclusive 0.565 | equivalence 0.417 | failed 0.000 ape_n(d, power = 0.80, claim = "equivalence", sesoi = 0.05,       nsim = 500, seed = 2) #> powerape required sample size -- equivalence claim #>   n = 3584 for 80% target power (confirmed 0.855, MCSE 0.008) #>   assumed true APE +0.0000, sesoi 0.050, 95% CI, probit #>   search: 4 step(s); confirmed in 1 round(s) at nsim = 2000. cv <- ape_curve(d, n = seq(500, 3500, by = 750), claim = "equivalence",                 sesoi = 0.05, nsim = 300, seed = 3) plot(cv, target_power = 0.80)

what: Specifying and pinning an interaction design
title: Power for average interaction effects (AIEs)
text: Add moderator DGP; index includes mains interaction. Pinning happens effect-size units via set_aie(), takes three explicit anchors: main_focal, main_moderator – conditional--reference APEs: APE variable held reference value (0 binary variables); target – AIE . binary--binary design exactly bijection four counterfactual cell rates: baseline p00, p10 = p00 + main_focal, p01 = p00 + main_moderator, p11 = p00 + main_focal + main_moderator + AIE. Feasibility checked every step (four cell rates must stay inside (0, 1); continuous variables AIE plateaus interaction coefficient), errors reporting attainable range.
code: library(powerape)  d <- ape_dgp(model = "probit",              focal = pa_var("treat", "binary", p = 0.5),              moderator = pa_var("female", "binary", p = 0.55),              covariates = list(pa_var("age", "normal", mean = 45, sd = 12)),              baseline = 0.30, signal = 0.10) d <- set_aie(d, target = 0.08, main_focal = 0.10, main_moderator = 0.03) d #> powerape DGP -- probit #>   focal: treat (binary, p = 0.50) #>   moderator: female (binary, p = 0.55) (focal-by-moderator interaction included) #>   covariates: age (normal, mean 45.00, sd 12.00)  #>   baseline P(Y=1 | reference) = 0.300, nuisance signal (latent pseudo-R2) = 0.100 #>   true AIE pinned at +0.0800 (beta_int = 0.2044) #>   main APEs at reference: treat +0.100 (beta = 0.2857), female +0.030 (beta = 0.0891)

title: Power Analysis for Average Partial Effects
text: Binary continuous focal variables (discrete-change average-derivative APEs), plateau-aware inversion informative feasibility errors. Interaction designs: pin average interaction effect — ginteff estimand — set_aie(); internal AIE unit-tested reproduce ginteff exactly four variable-type pairs. Three covariate routes: parametric marginals Gaussian copula, pilot-data resampling (ape_dgp_empirical()), fitted pilot model (ape_dgp_from_fit()). Robustness sweeps (ape_robust()): worst-case power insurance-premium sample size n_max contextual assumptions, spirit Hancock & Feng (2025). Citable output: power_statement() renders result self-contained methods paragraph grants preregistrations. Monte Carlo honesty: every power estimate carries MCSE; failed fits count claim, never silently dropped.

title: Specify a DGP from a fitted pilot model — ape_dgp_from_fit
code: set.seed(1) pilot <- data.frame(treat = rbinom(600, 1, 0.5),                     age = rnorm(600, 45, 12)) pilot$y <- rbinom(600, 1, pnorm(-0.6 + 0.3 * pilot$treat + 0.01 * pilot$age)) fit <- glm(y ~ treat + age, binomial("probit"), pilot) d <- ape_dgp_from_fit(fit, focal = "treat") d <- set_ape(d, target = 0.10) d #> powerape DGP -- probit (empirical covariates) #>   focal: treat (binary, p = 0.48) [resampled jointly with covariates] #>   covariates: age  #>   pilot rows: 600 (resampled with replacement) #>   pilot model: y ~ treat + age (nuisance coefficients lifted; focal coefficient re-solved) #>   baseline P(Y=1 | reference) = 0.404, nuisance signal (latent pseudo-R2) = 0.032 #>   true APE pinned at +0.1000 (beta_focal = 0.2571, implied P(Y=1 | focal=1) = 0.504)

what: Required sample size for a target power — ape_n
title: Required sample size for a target power — ape_n
text: Search plus confirmation. pilot run estimates SE scale (SE ~ c/sqrt(n)), normal-approximation formula proposes n, simulation proposal verifies adjusts estimated power within Monte Carlo precision goal. default confirmation stage re-measures candidate nsim_confirm replications accepts confirmed power max(0.005, 1.5 * MCSE) goal, pushing n upward otherwise (three rounds). confirmation never trims n overshoot – slight overshoot conservative direction sample-size planning. returned power MCSE come confirmation run. Works APE AIE designs alike.

title: Robustness sweep over contextual assumptions (worst-case power and n_max) — ape_robust
text: Power computed single guess contextual inputs – baseline rate, nuisance signal, covariate dependence – fragile (Hancock & Feng, 2025). ape_robust() re-runs power analysis scenario grid inputs reports per-scenario power, worst case, (optionally) n_max: sample size reaches target power worst scenario – insurance-premium n.

title: Robustness sweep over contextual assumptions (worst-case power and n_max) — ape_robust
text: dgp powerape_dgp set_ape() set_aie(). n Total sample size simulated study. claim "minimum" (default), "detect", "equivalence". sesoi Smallest effect size interest, APE units. Required "minimum" "equivalence"; optional "detect" (supplied, outcome table still broken ). conf CI level (default 0.95). nsim Number simulation replications. seed Optional seed (caller's RNG state preserved). vary Named list scenario values contextual inputs. Parametric route: baseline, signal, correlation (scalar); empirical route: baseline, signal. length-2 element expanded grid_points equally spaced values; longer vectors used -. Scenarios full factorial grid. pin "ape" (re-invert per scenario) "coefficients" (hold coefficients, let implied effect drift). grid_points Grid size used expand length-2 vary elements. nmax Run n_max search worst scenario (default TRUE). nmax_power Target power n_max search (default 0.90).

title: Robustness sweep over contextual assumptions (worst-case power and n_max) — ape_robust

title: Robustness sweep over contextual assumptions (worst-case power and n_max) — ape_robust
text: Two pinning modes (DESIGN.md section 3.3): pin = "ape" (default): inversion re-run every scenario, true effect stays planning value precision channel varies. Scenarios target infeasible reported , dropped silently. pin = "coefficients": effect coefficients stay base-case values contextual calibration redone; implied true effect drifts reported per scenario. Claim-boundary guards relaxed purpose – showing scenario collapses power point.

title: powerape 1.1.0
text: ape_n() gains high-precision confirmation stage: default (confirm = TRUE) candidate n re-measured nsim_confirm = 4 * nsim replications accepted confirmed power within max(0.005, 1.5 * MCSE) goal, pushing n upward otherwise (overshoot never trimmed – conservative direction). returned power MCSE come confirmation run; search history gains stage column. confirm = FALSE restores fast single-stage search. Validation battery added (tests/testthat/test-exact-power.R project-level battery): simulated power matches exact finite-sample power engine’s decision rule – computed triple binomial enumeration saturated case – within Monte Carlo error, detection, minimum-effect, equivalence claims. Cross-checks power.prop.test(), Stata power twoproportions, pwr (arcsine), Hsieh’s logistic-regression formulas (powerMediation) agree.

title: powerape 1.0.0
text: Pilot-model route: ape_dgp_from_fit() lifts covariate rows nuisance coefficients fitted binomial glm; focal coefficient re-solved APE units set_ape(). Optional baseline override. Four vignettes: minimum-effect workflow, classic SESOI detection analysis, equivalence testing, average interaction effects. Validation: APE point estimates delta-method SEs match Stata margins, dydx() ~4e-7 fixed data. pkgdown site hex logo.

title: powerape 0.3.0
text: Average interaction effects: set_aie() pins moderated DGP three explicit anchors (conditional--reference main-effect APEs plus target AIE); internal AIE estimator covers four variable-type pairs reproduces ginteff exactly (estimates SEs) fixed data. ape_robust(): scenario sweeps contextual assumptions pin--APE / pin--coefficients modes, worst-case power, insurance-premium sample size n_max (Hancock & Feng, 2025). power_statement(): renders result citable methods paragraph.

title: powerape 0.2.0
text: Continuous (normal) focal variables: average-derivative APE plateau-aware inversion feasibility reporting. Empirical-covariate route: ape_dgp_empirical() resamples pilot rows (focal jointly column, independently pa_var). Validation: APE estimates SEs match marginaleffects fixed data; simulated power matches Stata power twoproportions analytics.

title: powerape 0.1.0
text: Initial engine: probit/logit, binary focal variable, Gaussian-copula covariates, APE-unit inversion feasibility checks, CI-based claims (detect, minimum, equivalence; Riesthuis, 2024), ape_power(), ape_curve(), ape_n(), Monte Carlo SEs throughout.
